# What nudl removes

<!-- Generated by docs/make_rules_doc.py from src/rules.json. Do not edit by hand. -->

nudl strips **only** the keys on this page. Every other query parameter — including
ones nobody has thought of yet — is left untouched. That is what keeps it from
breaking links.

Matching is on the parameter **key**, case-insensitively, and never on its value.

## Removed everywhere

These ride along to whatever site you land on, so they are stripped on every host.

`^utm_.*$` `fbclid` `gclid` `dclid` `gbraid` `wbraid` `msclkid` `ttclid` `twclid` `li_fat_id` `yclid` `rdt_cid` `epik` `_openstat` `mc_eid` `mc_cid` `igshid` `igsh` `vero_id` `vero_conv` `_hsenc` `_hsmi` `oly_enc_id` `oly_anon_id` `^ss_.*$` `icid` `mkt_tok`

`^utm_.*$` is an anchored regex: it matches `utm_source`, `utm_medium`, `utm_campaign`,
`utm_term`, `utm_content` and any other `utm_` key, but **not** `utm` used as a value.

## Redirect wrappers unwrapped

nudl pulls the real destination out of these and throws the wrapper away. It does this
**locally**, by decoding the parameter — never by following the link.

| Wrapper | Target parameter |
| --- | --- |
| `l.facebook.com/l.php` | `u` |
| `lm.facebook.com/l.php` | `u` |
| `l.messenger.com/l.php` | `u` |
| `l.instagram.com` | `u` |
| `google.com/url` | `q` |
| `google.com/url` | `url` |
| `out.reddit.com` | `url` |
| `steamcommunity.com/linkfilter` | `url` |
| `t.umblr.com/redirect` | `z` |

## Never stripped — on purpose

These **look** like trackers. Removing them breaks the link, so nudl leaves them alone.
Each has a test in `src/tests/test_clean.py` so nobody helpfully adds them later.

| Parameter | Site | Why it stays |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `si` | Spotify | Share id. Removing it has broken shared-playlist flows. (YouTube's `si` is only a tracker, and is stripped.) |
| `sk` | Medium | **Friend-link token.** Strip it and you paywall the article. |
| `hash` | eBay | Identifies the item. Only the `_trk*` params there are tracking. |
| `img_index` | Instagram | Which photo in the carousel. |
| `sid` | Booking.com | Session id. |
| `context` | Reddit | How many parent comments to show. |
| `keywords` | Amazon | On `/s?keywords=` this **is** the search query. |
| `check_in / check_out` | Airbnb | The actual booking dates. |
| `v / t / list / index` | YouTube | Video, timestamp, playlist, position. |
| `q / page / id` | everywhere | Never on the list. Unknown keys are always kept. |

## Also never touched

- **Signed URLs.** Any query containing `sig`, `signature`, `hmac`, `token`, `expires`,
  `policy`, or an `X-Amz-*` / `X-Goog-*` / `X-Ms-*` key is returned **completely**
  unchanged. Signed URLs sign the whole query — removing any parameter turns the link
  into a 403.
- **Referral parameters** (`ref` `refid` `referrer` `referral`) are off by default.
  Turn them on with `strip_referral` in `config.json`.
- **Shorteners** (`bit.ly`, `t.co`, …). Expanding them would mean a network request,
  which would leak the link and can burn one-time URLs. Returned unchanged.

27 global keys · 91 site-specific keys across 17 sites · 9 redirect wrappers.
